'''NewSpace India Limited''' ('''NSIL''') is a [[Public Sector Undertakings in India|Public Sector Undertaking]] (PSU) of the [[Government of India]], under the [[Department of Space]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2023-03-29 |title=Army set to get its own satellite worth ₹3,000 crore by 2026 |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/army-set-to-get-its-own-satellite-worth-rs-3-000-crore-by-2026-101680100260858.html |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en |archive-date=8 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230608145156/https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/army-set-to-get-its-own-satellite-worth-rs-3-000-crore-by-2026-101680100260858.html |url-status=live }}</ref> NSIL is responsible for producing, assembling and integrating the launch vehicle with the help of industry consortium. It was established on 6 March 2019 under the administrative control of the [[Department of Space]] (DoS) and the [[Companies Act 2013]]. The main objective of NSIL is to scale up private sector participation in Indian space programmes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://smartinvestor.business-standard.com/market/Marketnews-584409-storydet-Isros_new_commercial_arm_NewSpace_India_officially_inaugurated.htm#.XWU5b-OA7Dc|title=ISRO's new commercial arm NewSpace India officially inaugurated|publisher=The Smart Investor|date=2019-08-27|website=smartinvestisor.business-standard.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190827142458/https://smartinvestor.business-standard.com/market/Marketnews-584409-storydet-Isros_new_commercial_arm_NewSpace_India_officially_inaugurated.htm|archive-date=2019-08-27|access-date=2019-08-27}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) - ISRO |url=https://www.isro.gov.in/about-isro/newspace-india-limited-nsil |access-date=2022-04-30 |website=www.isro.gov.in |archive-date=19 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220319195714/https://www.isro.gov.in/about-isro/newspace-india-limited-nsil |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Narasimhan |first=T. E. |date=2019-07-05 |title=Budget 2019: FM hikes Dept of Space outlay, pushes for commercialisation |publisher=Business Standard India |url=https://www.business-standard.com/budget/article/budget-2019-fm-hikes-dept-of-space-outlay-pushes-for-commercialisation-119070500973_1.html |access-date=2019-08-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190827143353/https://www.business-standard.com/budget/article/budget-2019-fm-hikes-dept-of-space-outlay-pushes-for-commercialisation-119070500973_1.html |archive-date=27 August 2019}}</ref>

== Objectives ==
NSIL was set up with the following objectives:<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=192201|title=NewSpace India Limited|date=24 Jul 2019|access-date=26 August 2019|publisher=Press Information Bureau, Government of India|archive-date=26 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190826093945/https://pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx%3Frelid%3D192201|url-status=live}}</ref>

* Transfer of Small Satellite technology to industry: NSIL will obtain license from DoS/ISRO and sub-license the same to industry
* Manufacture of [[Small Satellite Launch Vehicle]] (SSLV) in collaboration with private sector
* Production of [[Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle]] (PSLV) through Indian industry
* Production and marketing of Space-based products and services, including launch and application
* Transfer of technology developed by ISRO Centres and constituent units of DoS
* Marketing of spin-off technologies and products/services, both in India and abroad

==Contracts==
In 2022, NSIL executed a contract with [[Eutelsat OneWeb#OneWeb satellite constellation|OneWeb]] to launch 36 satellites to [[low Earth orbit]] for their [[satellite internet constellation]]. NSIL again successfully deployed another set of 36 OneWeb satellites on 26 March 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://oneweb.net/resources/successful-launch-36-oneweb-satellites-isronsil-marks-key-milestone-enable-global|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230326102616/https://oneweb.net/resources/successful-launch-36-oneweb-satellites-isronsil-marks-key-milestone-enable-global|title=Successful launch of 36 OneWeb Satellites with ISRO/NSIL marks key milestone to enable global connectivity|date=27 March 2023|archive-date=26 March 2023|access-date=27 March 2023|publisher=[[OneWeb]]|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-26 |title=PM Modi congratulates ISRO for launch of 36 satellites |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/pm-modi-congratulates-isro-for-launching-batch-of-36-satellites-101679834524557.html |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en |archive-date=26 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230526050255/https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/pm-modi-congratulates-isro-for-launching-batch-of-36-satellites-101679834524557.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Kandavel |first=Sangeetha |date=2023-03-26 |title=ISRO puts 36 OneWeb satellites in orbit |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/science/isro-successfully-launches-heaviest-payload-rocket-mission-lvm3-m3-oneweb-india-2-carrying-satellites/article66663592.ece |access-date=2023-03-31 |issn=0971-751X |archive-date=7 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230607015045/https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/science/isro-successfully-launches-heaviest-payload-rocket-mission-lvm3-m3-oneweb-india-2-carrying-satellites/article66663592.ece |url-status=live }}</ref>

The [[Ministry of defence|Ministry of Defence]] signed a ₹3,000-crore agreement with NSIL, a subsidiary of [[ISRO]], for the procurement of the advanced communication satellite, GSAT 7B, to meet the requirements of the Indian Army.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ministry of Defence signs 3 contracts worth Rs 5,400 crore to boost defence capabilities |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/ministry-of-defence-signs-3-contracts-worth-rs-5400-crore-to-boost-defence-capabilities-2353254-2023-03-30 |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=India Today |date=30 March 2023 |language=en |archive-date=10 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230410135652/https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/ministry-of-defence-signs-3-contracts-worth-rs-5400-crore-to-boost-defence-capabilities-2353254-2023-03-30 |url-status=live }}</ref>

An agreement was reached between NSIL and [[Arianespace]] for a long-term collaboration to enable satellite launch missions. As part of the Memorandum of Understanding, [[Ariane 6]] of Arianespace and the [[medium-lift launch vehicle]] [[LVM3]] of ISRO will answer the demand for launching larger communication or earth observation satellites as well as satellites for mega constellations, thereby satisfying the needs of the global launch service market.<ref>{{Cite news |last= |date=2024-01-31 |title=NSIL signs MoU with French company for long-term partnership to support satellite launch missions |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/nsil-signs-mou-with-french-company-for-long-term-partnership-to-support-satellite-launch-missions/article67795638.ece |access-date=2024-02-03 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

A launch service agreement has been signed by Space Machines Company and NSIL on 26 June 2024 for the launch of second Optimus spacecraft aboard the [[Small Satellite Launch Vehicle|SSLV]] in 2026. The mission will tackle the issue of [[space debris]] piling up around Earth, which poses a threat to astronaut safety as well as upcoming space missions. The mission is a component of the International Space Investment India Projects program and is supported by the [[Australian Space Agency]] with grant of $8.5 million.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-06-27 |title=Isro's arm NSIL to launch largest-ever Australian sat with its new rocket |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/isros-arm-nsil-to-launch-largest-ever-australian-sat-with-its-new-rocket/articleshow/111296126.cms |access-date=2024-06-28 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> Following the inaugration of a new NSIL facility in [[GIFT City|GIFT city]], [[Gujarat]], NSIL signed a contract with GalaxEye in February 2026 towards reselling under lincence satellite data and  solutions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Inauguration of new NSIL office at GIFT City, Gandhinagar, Gujarat |url=https://www.isro.gov.in/inaugurationNSIL.html |access-date=2026-02-13 |website=www.isro.gov.in}}</ref>
